title: Post-tonsillectomy haemorrhage
logic: Any fresh bleeding from mouth or nose, repeated swallowing in a sleeping child, or vomited blood within 14 days of tonsillectomy/adenoidectomy — even if it has apparently stopped
action: Treat as an emergency: admit, IV access and group-and-save, keep nil by mouth, senior ENT/surgical review; a 'herald bleed' that stopped still mandates observation because it may precede major haemorrhage; theatre for arrest of bleeding if any ongoing loss

title: Stridor or impending airway obstruction
logic: Stridor at rest, drooling, tripod posture, rising respiratory rate with falling conscious level, or oxygen desaturation in a patient with neck swelling, deep neck infection, airway foreign body or post-thyroid/neck surgery haematoma
action: Critical alert: do not lie the patient flat, do not attempt blind instrumentation; summon the most senior airway-capable clinicians; for post-operative neck haematoma open the wound at the bedside to release the clot; prepare surgical airway kit in parallel with intubation attempts

title: Tracheostomy tube blockage or displacement
logic: Tracheostomised patient with sudden respiratory distress, inability to pass a suction catheter, loss of airflow at the tube, or surgical emphysema
action: Follow the bedside emergency algorithm: remove inner cannula, suction, deflate cuff, remove the tube if obstruction persists (fresh stoma: use stay sutures/dilators), oxygenate face AND stoma; every ward accepting a tracheostomy must display the algorithm and stock a spare tube, one size smaller, and dilators at the bed

title: Tonsillitis episode-frequency criteria check
logic: Tonsillectomy booked for recurrent tonsillitis AND documented episode history does not reach approximately 7 episodes in 1 year, 5 per year over 2 years, or 3 per year over 3 years
action: Prompt the surgeon to record either the qualifying documented episode count or an explicit alternative indication (obstruction, quinsy recurrence, suspected neoplasm, febrile convulsions with tonsillitis); listing proceeds with the justification captured

title: Pre-mastoidectomy hearing and facial nerve baseline
logic: Mastoidectomy or middle-ear surgery booked AND (no pre-operative hearing assessment recorded OR no pre-operative facial nerve status recorded)
action: Block theatre listing until baseline audiometry (or documented reason none was obtainable, with tuning-fork findings) and facial nerve function are on the record — both are medicolegal baselines for recognised complications

title: Antibiotic prophylaxis for clean-contaminated head and neck surgery
logic: Procedure entering the upper aerodigestive mucosa (tonsillectomy excluded per local policy, but including deep neck drainage, mastoid, laryngeal and tracheostomy surgery) AND no prophylactic antibiotic recorded before incision
action: Prompt for a prophylactic agent with streptococcal and anaerobic cover per local formulary at induction; for established abscesses continue therapeutic (not just prophylactic) antibiotics and adjust to culture

title: First-72-hour tracheostomy observations
logic: New tracheostomy formed within the previous 72 hours
action: Schedule hourly airway checks initially (tube patency, secretions, cuff pressure once per shift, stoma site, surgical emphysema), continuous pulse oximetry, humidification; verify bedside safety equipment each shift and record the check

title: Overnight observation after adenotonsillectomy for obstructive symptoms
logic: Adenotonsillectomy performed for obstructive sleep-disordered breathing OR child under 3 years OR severe obstructive symptoms documented pre-operatively
action: Do not day-case: schedule overnight admission with pulse oximetry, given the elevated risk of post-obstructive airway events on the first night

title: Mastoid cavity lifelong surveillance
logic: Canal-wall-down mastoidectomy recorded AND no future cavity-care appointment exists at discharge
action: Auto-book pack removal at 2-3 weeks and recurring (at least annual) cavity inspection/microsuction; flag defaulters — an unattended cavity accumulates debris and infection, and recurrent cholesteatoma must be excluded

title: Post-bronchoscopy review after airway foreign body
logic: Rigid bronchoscopy for foreign body completed, especially for vegetable matter or delayed presentation
action: Review within 48 hours for fever or respiratory symptoms and again at 2 weeks; arrange chest radiograph if symptomatic — retained fragments and post-obstructive pneumonia are the key late risks
